scan_notes: Reviewed exact HEAD `114caf7c19fa767b444861703d408cf8c9feb2d6` against base `abbb8e4f6fd9a8410e4b9179256f9fca2d9f61ab`; worktree was clean. The three warned-about stale findings are absent at HEAD. Under normal READ COMMITTED boot behavior, fresh/prod create the marker without changing rows; dev demotes exactly the three named canaries; subsequent boots and post-migration operator promotions are preserved. The DO statement is one implicit transaction despite autocommit. `torque_app` owns application objects after `REASSIGN OWNED`; moreover, the preceding `ALTER TABLE clients` already requires ownership, so `COMMENT ON COLUMN` introduces no distinct privilege failure. PostgreSQL confirms that COMMENT requires ownership and locks the object ([COMMENT documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-comment.html)). All named readers handle 0 correctly: the registry badges but retains canaries, `real_product_codes()` and the workbook exclude them, the queue never classifies them real, and page resolution deliberately keeps non-demo canaries routable. `git grep` finds 104 remaining `_REAL_PRODUCTS` matches across 40 files; I found them historical, retrospective, or explicitly superseded—not actionable instructions. Fact-check passed, and citation-resolution/cited-test guards passed 27 tests. Database-backed canary tests could not run because the sandbox denied localhost PostgreSQL connections; no assertion body executed.

findings.title: Advisory recheck is unsafe outside READ COMMITTED
findings.evidence: `PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(13551351); IF NOT EXISTS (...) THEN UPDATE ...; COMMENT ...;` assumes the post-lock query sees the first boot's commit, but the connection does not pin READ COMMITTED. PostgreSQL documents that fresh per-query snapshots expose new commits under READ COMMITTED, while REPEATABLE READ retains the transaction snapshot ([SPI snapshot behavior](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/spi-spi-execute.html)).
findings.failure_scenario: If the database or `torque_app` has `default_transaction_isolation = 'repeatable read'`, two rollout tasks can establish snapshots before either commits. The second waits for the advisory lock but still sees its old snapshot afterward, concludes the comment is absent, and repeats the UPDATE. An operator promotion committed between the two migrations can therefore be reverted to 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly establish READ COMMITTED on the init_db session before this DO block, or fail closed unless `current_setting('transaction_isolation')` is `read committed`. Add a concurrent repeatable-read control.

findings.title: Atomicity test passes when UPDATE and marker are split
findings.evidence: After `init_db()`, the test only verifies both final effects: `assert _marker_exists(conn)` and that the three rows equal 0. It neither injects a failure between UPDATE and COMMENT nor verifies that both occupy one `_PG_MIGRATIONS` entry.
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit splits UPDATE and COMMENT into separate tuple entries. Every test still passes on successful boots, but if COMMENT then fails, autocommit leaves the backfill committed without its marker; a later boot can rerun it and undo an operator promotion.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert structurally that the guarded UPDATE and COMMENT are in one migration entry, or use a fault/role setup where COMMENT fails after UPDATE and verify neither effect commits. Also explicitly assert that a zero-row first boot creates the marker.

findings.title: New test docstring shows invalid tenant-update syntax
findings.evidence: The text says `torque-admin tenant update <slug> --real`, while the parser requires `tenant update --slug SLUG`; line 192 of the same file uses the correct form.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader copies the documented command and argparse rejects `<slug>` as an unexpected positional argument, so the intended operator promotion is not applied.

overall_explanation: The implementation satisfies the stated migration and reader behavior in the documented production configuration, and the citation sweep leaves no actionable `_REAL_PRODUCTS` reference. Reservations are the unstated transaction-isolation dependency, an atomicity test that does not constrain the claimed property, and one incorrect CLI example.
